answer: Coupled action escrow. An agent’s actions are grouped into fixed-size coordination bundles; each bundle must be countersigned by a distinct counterparty drawn from a ferrous-weighted peer pool, where peers build weight only through completed bundles. A falcon flag on any peer revokes their countersignature eligibility across all bundles. Attackers need N distinct active peers per bundle, each with real completed history; a violet ledger records orphaned bundles, so unused identities incur recurring maintenance costs without payoff.
